assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines Katori's magic-wavelength lattice idea with Sr/Yb implementations and has pushed fractional uncertainties into the 1e-18 range, well beyond microwave caesium standards. It underpins the expected redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. As an atomic physicist I see a clear, concrete, high-impact discovery with a single coherent story.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice concept and led early Sr work; Jun Ye's group brought the platform to the highest accuracy and many-body clock regimes. Two laureates fit the supplied credit cleanly. Other groups (e.g. NIST, PTB, SYRTE) contributed to the field but are not in the credited names; the frequency comb itself was already recognised in 2005.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs reproduce and compare clocks at the 1e-18 level; the technology is mature and international metrology decisions are in progress, so recognition is timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the optical-clock achievement is judged distinct enough from the 2005 frequency-comb prize and from ion-clock work recognised in 2012.
Relative contributions of Katori versus Ye to the later accuracy records are not fully resolved by the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal showed how cold trapped ions with motional-mode coupling could implement quantum logic gates, and experiments with ion registers have since led to high-fidelity gates and early quantum processors. This is a foundational quantum-information achievement with clear lasting impact, building on, but distinct from, the 2012 prize for single-system control.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive theoretical proposal; Blatt's group provided leading experimental realisation of gates, entanglement and scalable ion-trap processors. The three-person configuration is plausible, though Wineland, Monroe and others (not credited here) also did important experiments, which I note as an allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Theory dates from 1995 and has been experimentally validated for nearly three decades by several independent groups; commercial and academic ion-trap machines exist. Timely, with the field now clearly established.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to recognise experimentalists beyond Blatt, since the credited list is limited.
Overlap with the Cirac-Zoller optical-lattice simulation work on a sibling ballot entry, which might require splitting the recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and the entanglement-based E91 protocol established quantum cryptography with security guaranteed by quantum mechanics. This is a conceptually original idea with lasting impact on quantum communication, and it connects naturally to the 2022 recognition of entanglement experiments.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard invented BB84; Ekert independently proposed the entanglement-based approach linking security to Bell inequalities. The three credited names match a coherent trio of the founding concepts, though Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not in the credited list and is a known historical attribution point.
assessment.maturity: Protocols have been demonstrated over fibre and satellite links, with commercial systems and long-running experimental validation. Practical security (device imperfections) remains a field of ongoing work, but the principle is secure and well verified.
uncertainties: Stephen Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding contribution cannot be recognised because he is deceased and not in the credited names.
A near-duplicate ballot entry exists with teleportation emphasised; I rank only this QKD-focused entry.
Possible partial overlap with the 2022 prize may lower urgency.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mapping the acoustic peaks of the CMB with WMAP and Planck fixed the cosmological parameters to percent precision and established the concordance model. This is a landmark observational and theoretical achievement. The 2006 prize recognised COBE and the 2019 prize Peebles's theoretical framework, so the precision-era contribution is distinct.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across a large collaboration with five named people. I would put forward Bennett as WMAP PI, Spergel for the parameter analysis, and Sunyaev for early theory of acoustic oscillations and secondary effects; Page and Puget are also strong but only three can be chosen, so the configuration is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, confirmed by multiple independent satellites and ground and balloon experiments, with stable interpretation.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among WMAP, Planck and ground-based leaders is unresolved.
The committee may consider the field already well covered by 2006 and 2019.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos and the first source associations (TXS 0506+056, the Galactic plane) opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies, a technically ambitious experiment with original science return.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the project; Karle was a central figure in building and leading the detector. The two credited names support a prize pair, though the large collaboration and other pioneers (AMANDA, Baikal, ANTARES) mean allocation is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is established, but source identification is still developing; the field is advanced but not yet fully mature. Recognition is plausible but arguably a few years early for source astronomy.
uncertainties: Source-level evidence is limited to a few associations.
Allocation relative to broader neutrino-telescope pioneers is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry turned matter waves into precision sensors, giving measurements of gravity, rotation and fundamental constants. As an atomic theorist I regard the underlying coherence control as a deep demonstration of quantum mechanics with wide applications.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard and Bordé contributed early foundational demonstrations and theory; Kasevich developed the light-pulse interferometer and precision applications. The credited trio is reasonable, but Chu and others in the lineage were already recognised in 1997 for cooling, and several groups contributed in parallel.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups and now moving into field use; maturity is high, though headline fundamental-physics results (e.g. G, equivalence principle tests) are still evolving.
uncertainties: Distinctness from the 1997 laser-cooling prize and from the 2001 BEC prize.
Credit among parallel early demonstrations may be disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect introduced Z2 topological insulators, a transformative concept in condensed matter that spawned a large field. The 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions and the integer quantum Hall effect, so this is a related but distinct discovery.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group provided the experimental HgTe confirmation (with Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang proposing the HgTe route, who are not credited here). This creates an attribution risk with credit omitted from the list.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed experimentally and theoretically across multiple material systems; maturity is high.
uncertainties: Important contributors (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang; Fu and Kane for the 3D case) are not among the credited names.
Overlap with the sibling ballot entry on quantum anomalous Hall transport.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory made it possible to treat strongly correlated electron materials non-perturbatively and underlies modern computational approaches to Mott physics and correlated materials. It is a widely used framework with large lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar developed the DMFT mapping onto impurity models and Vollhardt (with Metzner and Müller-Hartmann on the infinite-dimension limit) made foundational contributions. The three credited names are reasonable but omit Metzner, who is a notable allocation concern.
assessment.maturity: Validated by decades of use and comparison with experiments and other methods, though it is a method with approximation limits; the discovery is a theoretical tool rather than a single observed phenomenon, and the Nobel tradition for such methods is mixed.
uncertainties: Whether a computational/theoretical method fits the Nobel criteria as a discovery.
Omitted contributors such as Metzner and Müller-Hartmann.
